title: Splice Repair of a Cabin Floor Seat Track in a Galley or Lavatory Zone

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Splice repair of a corroded cabin floor seat track section in a galley or lavatory zone, covering the cut-out limits, the splice plate installation and the seat fitting lock check that releases the run.

sections.purpose: This task repairs a corroded section of cabin floor seat track by cutting out the damaged length and installing a splice plate, and confirms that a seat fitting locks repeatably along the repaired run.
sections.job_setup_note: Only one splice is permitted at any station and a run that already carries a splice at the intended position must be replaced instead of repaired. Record the station of every existing splice in the run before you start. The floor beam beneath the cut-out must be inspected once the track is lifted, because corrosion that has passed through the track usually has.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove the seats, the monument and the floor panels over the full length of the affected run. 2. Record the station of every existing splice in the run. CAUTION: ONLY ONE SPLICE IS PERMITTED AT A STATION. IF A SPLICE IS ALREADY PRESENT AT THE INTENDED POSITION THE RUN MUST BE REPLACED AND THIS REPAIR MUST NOT BE USED. 3. Clean the track and remove the sealant from the fastener line. 4. Define the extent of the corrosion by detailed visual inspection and confirm it with a dye penetrant inspection at both ends. 5. Mark the cut-out to the limits in the instructions, keeping the cut clear of a floor beam crossing. WARNING: PROTECT THE SYSTEMS BELOW THE FLOOR BEFORE ANY CUTTING. THE WIRING AND THE DUCTING UNDER THE CABIN FLOOR ARE DIRECTLY BENEATH THE TRACK. 6. Remove the track fasteners over the cut-out length and lift the section clear. 7. Inspect the floor beam and the web NOD599116-78 beneath the cut-out and report any corrosion. 8. Cut the replacement section and offer it up dry. 9. Install the splice plate FAR167574-60 at each end and check the fit with a feeler gauge. 10. Apply the protection scheme to all bare material. 11. Install the fasteners wet with sealant, working from the centre of the splice outwards. 12. Install the clip D5350122405771 at each floor beam crossing and the upper clip D5350121750926. 13. Check that a seat fitting locks and releases at ten positions along the repaired run, including both sides of each splice. 14. Seal the fastener line and restore the floor panels.
sections.close_out: Record the cut-out length, the splice stations and the seat fitting lock check result on the repair record. Reinstall the monument and the seats to the cabin layout. Report the repair to engineering so that the run history is maintained; a run may not carry more splices than the limit in the instructions.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The splice limit per run differs pre and post the corrosion-resistant track standard.

safety_precautions: Protect the systems below the floor before any cutting.
Record every existing splice station before you start.
Do not repair a run that already carries a splice at the intended position.
